cohort: The study included 156 patients who had undergone arterial ligation (bilateral uterine artery ligation or bilateral hypogastric artery ligation) for postpartum hemorrhage and a control group.
finding: Bilateral hypogastric artery ligation (BHAL) was significantly associated with a higher rate of preterm birth (32.2%) compared to bilateral uterine artery ligation (BUAL, 12.8%) and the control group (6%).
mod_finding: There was no significant difference between the groups in subsequent pregnancies in terms of the incidence of primary cesarean deliveries.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from January 2010 to June 2018.
